chunks: Mu‘āwiyah ibn ‘Ammār narrated from Abī ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

"Whoever gives water in a place where water is available is like one who frees a slave. And whoever gives water in a place where water is not available is like one who revives a soul. And whoever revives a soul,
"it is as though he has revived all of humanity."

key_terms.أَحْيَا: revived or gave life, meaning to save from destruction or death
key_terms.أَعْتَقَ: freed or emancipated, specifically a slave
key_terms.النَّاسَ جَمِيعًا: all people collectively; all of humanity
key_terms.الْمَاءَ: water, the essential resource being provided
key_terms.رَقَبَةً: a slave person, in the sense of one whose bondage is removed
key_terms.سَقَى: gave water; provided water for others to drink
key_terms.مَوْضِعٍ: a place or location where people may or may not have access to water

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for giving water to people according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the great virtue of providing water, especially where it is scarce and urgently needed. It compares giving water in ordinary circumstances to freeing a slave, and in conditions of scarcity to reviving a human life. The narration concludes with a Qur'anic expression emphasizing the immense moral value of saving life.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1724 - Mu'awiyah ibn Ammar narrated from Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as):

"Whoever gives water in a place where water is available is like one who frees a slave. And whoever gives water in a place where water is not available is like one who revives a soul. And whoever revives a soul,
it is as though they have revived all of humanity."
